summary: Hale & Kilburn was a Philadelphia furniture manufacturing company founded by Henry S. Hale and Cheney Kilburn. Its main business was producing railroad car seats for the rapidly expanding American railroads. The company was sold to J.P. Morgan & Co. in 1911 for $9 million.
one_line: Philadelphia furniture maker Hale & Kilburn, known for railroad car seats, sold to J.P. Morgan & Co. in 1911.
key_facts: Hale & Kilburn was a furniture manufacturing company based in Philadelphia.
Hale & Kilburn was founded by Henry S. Hale and Cheney Kilburn.
The primary business of Hale & Kilburn was the production of railroad car seats.
Hale & Kilburn's railroad car seats were supplied to the greatly expanding American railroad companies.
Hale & Kilburn was sold to J.P. Morgan & Co. in 1911.
The sale of Hale & Kilburn to J.P. Morgan & Co. in 1911 was for $9 million.
